correctness.rationale: The Schur-eigenvector projection formula is derived from centered diagonal moments. Its squared minor-axis is V-|c|²/V=4 det(C)/tr(C). Opposite-point symmetrization increases covariance by mm^T and the objective is strictly monotone on positive-definite covariance, forcing centered optimal laws. Unique rational one-variable optimization yields kappa* and Delta². A direct normalized companion vector constructs a nilpotent compression, and equality at every step forces the unique weight law and diagonal-phase orbit. The exact perpendicular rectangular limit agrees with the prior theorem; standalone deterministic script checks the projection witnesses and many trial distributions. Finite checking is supportive, not a proof of the continuum theorem.

value.rationale: The norm of a natural four-point normal spectral configuration is an operator-geometric invariant with a previously exact sharp rectangle case. Obliquity creates a genuine optimization parameter and changes the exact extremizer away from equal weights; the theorem gives a full two-real-parameter spectral formula and all extremizers, plus direct impact on the positive-block norm-excess problem.
